name: Direct novel-interest exploration and forecasting: verified evidence map
venue_year: Google RecSys 2024; UpliftRec SIGIR 2024; NNBR SIGIR 2023; User Feedback Alignment ACL Industry 2025; Personalized Interest Graphs RecSys 2025; CoEA, MLLM-serendipity, and BALANCE records [uncertain]
official_sources: Verified primary records: https://doi.org/10.1145/3640457.3688161 ; https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-industry.70/ ; https://doi.org/10.1145/3626772.3657736 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.08582 ; https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608803 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.01308 ; https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748133 . Authoritative records for the requested CoEA, 'Serendipitous Recommendation with MLLM', and SIGIR 2026 BALANCE labels were not located in the accessible ACM, ACL, DBLP, Crossref, OpenAlex, arXiv, or official-repository searches [uncertain].
release_and_license: The Google 2024 and ACL 2025 papers are publicly readable as paper/abstract records, but their production logs, interest taxonomy, models, and evaluation data are private. UpliftRec has a public arXiv paper and evaluates public Yahoo!R3, Coat, and KuaiRec data under each dataset's own terms; no official implementation repository was verified [uncertain]. NNBR has a public arXiv paper and uses Ta-Feng, dunnhumby, and Instacart, but the paper's original Instacart link is no longer live and each dataset has separate terms. The eBay PIG paper has a verified ACM DOI, but no public dataset or official code release was verified [uncertain]. CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE release and license are unverified [uncertain].
input_history: Google 2024 uses a user's established behavior and an industrial interest-cluster vocabulary; an LLM proposes high-level interests and a sequential recommender grounds them to items. ACL 2025 uses existing user behavior and hierarchical interest planning, with separate novelty-focused and user-alignment LLMs. UpliftRec uses observational interaction history, user covariates, category exposure ratios, and backend recommender embeddings. NNBR uses an ordered sequence of prior purchase baskets. PIG appears, from the verified title and references, to construct theme-driven personalized interest graphs from user behavior, but the exact input window and graph construction were not recoverable from a primary full text [uncertain]. CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE inputs are unverified [uncertain].
prediction_target: Google 2024 generates a next high-level novel interest description/cluster and then recommends items constrained to that cluster. ACL 2025 plans novel interests/content and selects best-of-n candidates for alignment before deployment. UpliftRec optimizes the category composition of a top-N slate by estimating CTR under alternative category exposure ratios; it is an intervention policy, not a passive future-label forecaster. NNBR ranks the novel items in the user's next purchase basket. PIG's exact supervised target is unverified [uncertain]. CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE targets are unverified [uncertain].
novel_interest_definition: Google 2024 explicitly targets novel interests outside the feedback loop while constraining generated interests to designer-defined interest clusters. ACL 2025 decouples novelty from user alignment and seeks content beyond established preferences. UpliftRec calls an item unexpected when its category is not among the user's top three historical interaction categories; this is not the same as a category absent from all history. NNBR defines an explore item as an item never consumed in any prior basket and the target basket contains only such items; it does not require a new category. PIG, CoEA, MLLM-serendipity, and BALANCE operational definitions are unverified [uncertain].
novelty_granularity_and_reference_window: Google 2024: interest-cluster level relative to industrial behavioral history, but the exact lookback window and cluster hierarchy are private [uncertain]. ACL 2025: planned interest/content novelty relative to established preferences, with the exact reference window private [uncertain]. UpliftRec: item category outside the user's historical top three categories, not history-absent category. NNBR: item-level novelty relative to all input baskets. PIG: graph-node/theme granularity [uncertain]. CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE: unverified [uncertain].
interest_onset_definition: Google 2024 and ACL 2025 validate exploration through downstream online enjoyment/watch activity and active-user outcomes, so deployment response rather than offline first occurrence is the onset signal; exact event definitions are private [uncertain]. UpliftRec uses positive rating or watch-based outcomes and category CTR under exposure. NNBR uses first purchase of an item in the held-out next basket. None of the verified papers requires later repeated adoption as the definition of onset.
is_direct_match: Google 2024 and ACL 2025 are direct semantic-interest exploration methods, but the evidence is private online intervention rather than a reproducible history-to-future benchmark. NNBR is a direct history-to-future novelty task only at item granularity. UpliftRec is adjacent causal exploration because 'unexpected' means outside top-three categories rather than absent from history. PIG is adjacent/method inspiration until its target and evaluation can be checked [uncertain]. CoEA, MLLM-serendipity, and BALANCE cannot be classified beyond requested-candidate status without authoritative records [uncertain].
persistence_signal: Google 2024 reports online enjoyment, and ACL 2025 reports watch activity and active-user counts, but the accessible abstracts do not establish user-level repeat adoption of each newly explored interest [uncertain]. UpliftRec evaluates immediate randomized-test preference/CTR. NNBR observes only the next basket target. No verified work here cleanly separates a one-off novel response from persistent new-interest adoption.
method: Google 2024 is a hierarchical hybrid: LLM generation over predefined interest clusters followed by a transformer sequential recommender constrained to generated clusters. ACL 2025 uses hierarchical planning, inference-time scaling, separate novelty and alignment LLMs, and best-of-n selection. UpliftRec treats category exposure ratios as treatments, estimates group-level dose-response/treatment effects with inverse-propensity adjustment or a marginal-treatment-effect approximation, and solves a dynamic-programming allocation problem for the top-N slate. NNBR proposes a bidirectional transformer basket recommender with item/basket masking objectives and item-basket swapping. PIG method details are [uncertain]; CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE methods are [uncertain].
evaluation_protocol: Google 2024 uses an industrial live experiment and reports increased novel-interest exploration and user enjoyment; public offline splits, candidates, and metrics are unavailable. ACL 2025 uses live experiments with watch activity, active-user counts, and exploration diversity; public protocol details are limited. UpliftRec trains on biased observations and splits the randomized/unbiased component 50/50 for validation/test on Yahoo!R3, Coat, and KuaiRec; it reports Recall@K, NDCG@K, unexpected-category Recall@K, and unpopular-item Recall@K. NNBR samples users with 3-50 baskets, removes infrequent items, uses user-disjoint 80/20 train/test with 10% of training users for validation, repeats five splits, and reports Recall@K and NDCG@K over next novel items. PIG and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE protocols are [uncertain].
generalization_axis: Google 2024 and ACL 2025 test online responses of production users but do not expose user-disjoint, cold-category, or temporal backtest details. UpliftRec tests policy transfer from biased training observations to randomized ratings/watch outcomes for the same dataset populations. NNBR is user-disjoint but predicts next-basket items for users represented only by their own history; it is not a cold-category test. PIG and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE axes are [uncertain].
exposure_handling: Google 2024 and ACL 2025 intervene by serving recommendations online, but propensities and complete impression logs are private. UpliftRec explicitly models category exposure ratio as treatment, uses inverse propensity weighting, and evaluates on randomized/unbiased components; this is the strongest exposure-aware evidence in this set, though its causal assumptions and group-level effects do not identify an individual's latent unseen category. NNBR has purchase baskets without full contemporaneous exposure or non-purchase candidates, so unpurchased catalog items are not strict negatives. PIG and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE exposure handling is [uncertain].
main_findings_and_limits: The closest verified semantic-category work is Google's 2024/2025 line: it can generate cluster-level interests outside established preferences and improve online exploration alongside satisfaction, but neither data nor taxonomy is public, so it does not supply a reproducible forecasting benchmark. UpliftRec provides public exposure-aware evidence, but its unexpected-category label is outside the top three, not absent from history. NNBR is the cleanest reproducible future-novel target and reports that prior NBR progress is limited on explore items, but novelty is item-level and exposure is missing. PIG is potentially useful for structured interest representation, but only bibliographic identity was verified. Claims about CoEA, MLLM-serendipity, and BALANCE must remain unverified [uncertain].
scale: Google 2024 states an industrial platform serving billions of users, but analysis counts are private [uncertain]. ACL 2025 gives no public sample counts in the accessible abstract [uncertain]. UpliftRec reports Yahoo!R3: 15.4K users, 1.0K items, 125.1K positive and 167.9K negative training interactions; Coat: 290 users, 300 items, 1.9K positive and 5.1K negative; KuaiRec: 7.1K users, 10.7K items, 936.5K positive and 11.6M negative. NNBR processed data: Ta-Feng 13,858 users/11,997 items, dunnhumby 22,530/3,920, Instacart 19,435/13,897. PIG and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE scales are [uncertain].
stable_user_identity: Google 2024 and ACL 2025 necessarily use production user histories, but identifier duration is private. UpliftRec's benchmark users persist across biased and randomized components. NNBR retains per-user basket sequences and performs user-disjoint model evaluation. PIG identity duration and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE identities are [uncertain].
timestamps_and_order: NNBR has ordered baskets but the paper's processed protocol does not make absolute timestamp resolution central. UpliftRec uses biased versus randomized components rather than a documented chronological future split. Google 2024/ACL 2025 production chronology is private. PIG and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE chronology is [uncertain].
left_censoring_and_history_coverage: None of the verified methods proves that an interest absent from the observed window is new over the user's lifetime. Google/ACL history coverage is private; UpliftRec uses historical top-three categories, so sparse history directly changes 'unexpectedness'; NNBR restricts novelty to the observed prior baskets. All should be described as observed-history novelty, not ontological new interest.
item_semantics: Google 2024 uses language descriptions attached to predefined interest clusters and item grounding, but the vocabulary is private. ACL 2025 uses hierarchical interest planning but the ontology is private. UpliftRec uses dataset categories when available and otherwise proposes clustering recommender embeddings; Yahoo!R3 lacks category labels. NNBR's three experiments primarily use item IDs and basket co-occurrence, not a semantic category hierarchy. PIG likely uses textual theme/interest nodes [uncertain].
feedback_and_exposure: Google 2024: private live recommendations and enjoyment responses. ACL 2025: live recommendations, watch activity, active-user counts, and exploration diversity. UpliftRec: ratings or watch-time-derived positives, biased observations, randomized/unbiased evaluation data, category treatments, but not a public full production slate log. NNBR: purchase baskets without impressions. PIG and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE fields are [uncertain].
candidate_space: Google 2024 first limits generation to predefined interest clusters and then items within selected clusters, but catalog reconstruction is private. ACL 2025 candidate generation and availability are private [uncertain]. UpliftRec reallocates a top-N list across categories from backend candidates; full contemporaneous catalog and inventory are not reconstructed. NNBR evaluates fixed-size top-K novel-item ranking after preprocessing, not actual exposure candidates. PIG and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE are [uncertain].
taxonomy_and_opportunity_drift: No verified paper fully releases taxonomy versions, item launch times, inventory, geography, or whether a target category was available during history. Google interest clusters are designer-controlled but private; UpliftRec categories or embedding clusters may drift; NNBR item availability is not exposure-audited. This prevents separating user-interest emergence from catalog opportunity.
construct_h_f_ynew: For Google/ACL, the public material is insufficient to reconstruct H(u), F(u), or labels; only the method concept transfers. For UpliftRec, H(u) can be biased-history categories and F(u) randomized-test positives, but the paper's label is category not in top-3(H), not F-H; a CrossInterest reanalysis should require category absent from all H. For NNBR, H(u) is all items in prior baskets, F(u) is the next basket, and Y_new(u)=F(u) minus the union of H(u); a category-level variant requires trustworthy item taxonomy. PIG and CoEA/MLLM/BALANCE reconstruction is [uncertain].
leakage_and_missingness_risks: Major risks are finite-window left censoring, recommender-mediated MNAR exposure, future catalog/category availability, popularity and seasonality, using post-cutoff embeddings or clusters, and equating unobserved with disliked. Google/ACL cannot be audited from private logs. UpliftRec's randomized components help with exposure bias, but 'top-three' unexpectedness is history-frequency dependent. NNBR's purchase-only data lacks exposures and catalog opportunity; user-disjoint splitting does not remove left censoring.
recommended_role: Use Google 2024/ACL 2025 as the closest method and production-evidence references; use NNBR as the closest public label-construction and repeat/explore evaluation reference; use UpliftRec as causal/exposure-aware auxiliary methodology and public robustness evidence; use PIG as lower-priority structured-interest representation inspiration pending full-text verification. Do not rely on CoEA, MLLM-serendipity, or BALANCE until authoritative records are supplied or located [uncertain].
priority: High: Google 2024, ACL 2025, NNBR, and UpliftRec because together they cover semantic cluster exploration, alignment, item-level future novelty, and exposure-aware treatment effects. Medium: eBay PIG, because the verified title is relevant but task/evaluation details remain unavailable. Reject for evidence claims pending verification: CoEA, MLLM-serendipity, and BALANCE [uncertain].
verification_status: Primary-source verified: canonical titles/venues/DOIs for Google 2024, ACL 2025, UpliftRec, NNBR, and eBay PIG; abstracts and full arXiv text for ACL 2025, UpliftRec, and NNBR; Crossref/DBLP metadata for PIG. Partially verified: Google 2024 through the ACM/OpenAlex abstract record. Not verified: PIG full method/data details; any authoritative identity, venue record, or source for the requested CoEA, MLLM-serendipity, and SIGIR 2026 BALANCE labels [uncertain].
repeat_explore_and_persistence_audit: NNBR explicitly excludes every previously consumed item and is the only verified work here with a clean repeat-versus-explore item split. UpliftRec separates unexpected categories and unpopular items but does not define repeat versus first-ever category. Google/ACL optimize exploration but public reports do not expose a repeat/explore contingency table or per-interest persistence. None verifies sustained adoption with a later confirmation window.
evidence_quotes_or_schema_facts: Google 2024 abstract: the framework 'recommends the next novel interests' through language-represented interest clusters and grounds them to items. ACL 2025 abstract: it 'decouple[s] novelty and user-alignment' and selects best-of-n novelty proposals with a user-aligned LLM; live metrics include watch activity, active users, and exploration diversity. UpliftRec full text: treatment is category exposure ratio; Yahoo!R3, Coat, and KuaiRec contain biased and randomized/unbiased parts; an item is unexpected when its category is not in the user's top three historical categories. NNBR abstract: an explore item is one the user 'has not consumed before,' and the target basket contains only novel items. PIG bibliographic fact: 'Personalized Interest Graphs for Theme-Driven User Behavior,' RecSys 2025, DOI 10.1145/3705328.3748133.
sources: Google 2024 ACM DOI: https://doi.org/10.1145/3640457.3688161 ; ACL 2025 primary page/PDF: https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-industry.70/ ; UpliftRec ACM/arXiv: https://doi.org/10.1145/3626772.3657736 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.08582 ; NNBR ACM/arXiv: https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608803 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.01308 ; PIG ACM DOI: https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748133 ; DBLP PIG record: https://dblp.org/rec/conf/recsys/ZinmanCFBFE25 . No primary URLs verified for CoEA, MLLM-serendipity, or BALANCE [uncertain].
